title: First Arrival at the Prepared Configuration
statement: Let $l,W\in\mathbb{N}$, let $w_0,\ldots,w_{l-1}$ be Boolean words of length at most $W$, and let $\mathrm{tail}$ be any Boolean word; let $x$ be the packed encoding of the row followed by the trailer. There is a time $t\le 2|x|+3+l(3W+7)$ with $t>0$ such that the preparation machine started on $x$ has the specified loading configuration at time $t$, and at every earlier time $j<t$ its state is not the loader's final-counter entry state.
hypotheses_covered: A family of $l$ Boolean words, each of length at most $W$
replaced: For every row of field words of length at most $W$ and trailer, there is a strictly positive time, within the preparation ledger $2|x| + 3 + l(3W+7)$, at which the preparation machine first reaches the prepared seam with all fields parsed; native input copying and the dispatch ensure positivity even with zero fields.
